chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Halab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about the hunting of the falcon and the dog; if it hunts and kills its prey and eats from it, do we eat from its surplus or not?

He said: As for what the bird kills, do not eat it unless you slaughter it (recite the name of Allah); and as for what the dog kills and you have mentioned Allah's name upon it, then eat it even if it eats from it.

key_terms.تُذَكِّيَهُ: You slaughter it (by reciting the name of Allah)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling between eating prey killed by a falcon versus a dog in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of hunting by distinguishing between birds of prey, which require post-capture slaughter (dhakat) to render the meat halal, and trained dogs, whose kill is permissible upon the recitation of Bismillah even if they consume part of it. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that the dog's consumption does not invalidate the meat, provided the hunter's invocation was valid, emphasizing the role of the hunter's intention and recitation over the animal's action.
